text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English antiquary JOHN AUBREY, whose book "Brief Lives" was published 201 years after his death, was born in 1626.

British soldier and engineer EDWARD CLOSE, who built the Saint James Church of England church in Newcastle as a pledge for surviving the Peninsular War, (when NAPOLEON invaded Portugal and Spain), was born in 1790.

English missionary and journalist RALPH MANSFIELD, who wrote and published the first demographic study of the New South Wales colony, and also became Editor of the Sydney Gazette and Sydney Morning Herald, was born in 1799.
Scottish journalist WILLIAM DUNCAN, who became Editor of the Sydney Australasian Chronicle, was born in 1811.
English chemist SIR HENRY PERKIN, who synthesized the first artificial dye (aniline purple), was born on this day in 1838.
Australian botanist ELLEN BENHAM, the first woman academic at Adelaide University, was born on this day in 1871.

Australian aviator HENRY KAUPER, who invented the gearing that enabled a machine gun to be fired through an aircraft propeller in World War I, and who was also a pioneer radio broadcaster with 5AD, 5DN and 3BD, was born in 1888.
Russian dancer VASLAV NIJINSKY, whose career was cut short by mental illnes, was born in 1890.

American singer, dancer and actress LIZA MINNELLI (daughter of JUDY GARLAND) was born in 1946. One of her many husbands was the late Australian singer/songwriter PETER ALLEN. As a child she danced on stage while her mother sang. In 1972 she played the part of Sally Bowles in the film "Cabaret". Her other films included "New York, New York" in 1977 and in 1981 "Arthur". Her most successful album was "Liza With A Z" (1972).
British actress GOOGIE WITHERS, who married Australian actor JOHN MACCALLUM and moved to live in Australia, was born in 1917.
American playwright EDWARD ALBEE, whose best known work is "Who's Afraid Of Virginia Wolf?", was born in 1928.
Australian writer ANNE SUMMERS was born in 1945.
Australian pop singer JOHNNY YOUNG (Young Talent Time) was born in 1945.

US singer/guitarist/ songwriter JAMES TAYLOR was born in 1948. He had his first hit with "Fire And Rain" in 1970 and then had a monster hit with "You've Got A Friend" (1971), which was written by CAROLE KING. He had a hit with "Mockingbird", a duet with CARLY SIMON, to whom he was married for ten years from 1972. Other hits included "How Sweet It Is (To Be Loved By You)" (1975) and "Handy Man" (1977).
Co-founder of 'Iron Maiden' STEVE HARRIS was born in 1956. The UK bass player/ songwriter helped set up the group in 1976.
1789 : The United States Post Office was established.
1912 : JULIETTE GORDON LOW founded the Girl Guides in the
US.
1913 : Canberra became the Australian capital. In 1899 a

Royal Commission had been set up to choose a site for the national capital, and American architect WALTER BURLEY GRIFFIN won a competition to draw up a plan for the new city. The competition to find a name for the city included entries such as "KANGAREMU" and "AUSTRALIFIC", and the winning name was kept
Another JACKSON, MARLON was born in 1957.
** EVENTS **
1507 : CESARE BORGIA, Italian politician, cardinal and
adventurer, was killed in a battle with rebels of Navarre near Viana, Italy.

1925 : SUN YAT-SEN, Chinese revolutionary leader, died.
Known as the father of modern China, he became its first provisional president for a short time (1911-1912).
1930 : India's spiritual leader MAHATMA GANDHI began a
300 mile protest journey to defy the British law establishing a monopoly in producing salt.
1938 : ADOLF HITLER's troops marched into Austria, making
the country a German province.
1945 : Young German/Jewish diarist ANNE FRANK died in a
German concentration camp. The diary of her time in hiding was published in 1947.
1947 : United States President HARRY TRUMAN delivered a
speech to Congress, and using the phrase "Cold War", urged efforts to prevent the global spread of Communism.
1955 : CHARLIE "THE BIRD" PARKER, legendary jazz
musician, died.
1967 : Indonesian Congress stripped Dr SUKARNO of all
powers including the title of President. Gen. SUHARTO became acting president until after general elections in 1968.
1969 : The song "MRS ROBINSON" was voted Record Of The
Year, winning a Grammy for PAUL SIMON and ART GARFUNKEL.
1969 : PAUL MCCARTNEY married LINDA EASTMAN (who was a
descendant of GEORGE EASTMAN, the man who invented the Kodak camera).
1972 : The Australian Women's Electoral Lobby was formed.
1981 : The wife of Queensland's National Party leader was

endorsed by State Parliament to fill the Federal Senate vacancy caused by the resignation of DR GLEN SHIEL. Lady FLO BJELKE-PETERSEN's appointment caused a political upset as it was traditional for a candidate of the same political persuasion to fill any resulting vacancy.
1991 : SADDAM HUSSEIN's troops crushed a rebellion in
southern Iraq, where Shi'ite Muslims had been demanding their own separate state.
1994 : The Church of England broke with 460 years of male
dominance when it ordained its first women priests in Bristol Cathedral.
1996 : China began new war games in the Taiwan Strait in
a show of force that used jets and warships to drive home its warning to Taiwan not to seek independence.
